body:
For reference, the [AUR PKGBUILD](https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=starship)

All it does is get the source code tarball from GitHub, unpack it, then run 

```
cargo build --release --locked
cargo test --locked
```

@oblitum I'm 99% sure that this is an issue with here and not the AUR package, but let's be sure. If you [download the source code](https://github.com/starship/starship/releases), unpack it, and then run `cargo build --release` and `cargo test`, does this still happen?

If so, could you run `pacman -Qqe > pkglist.txt` and then either paste the contents here or (if they're too long) in a Gist or pastebin?

@chipbuster I noticed there's a binary linux asset there, why not grab from it? I'm asking because building from sources takes quite a time and increases rustup cache, which isn't small by the way.

The issue remains when running `cargo test` manually.

I just got this and one other similar test failure when building 0.11.0 on macOS

```
---- directory::directory_in_root stdout ----
thread 'directory::directory_in_root' panicked at 'assertion failed: `(left == right)`
  left: `"in \u{1b}[1;36m/etc\u{1b}[0m "`,
 right: `""`', tests/testsuite/directory.rs:81:5
note: Run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.

---- directory::home_directory stdout ----
thread 'directory::home_directory' panicked at 'assertion failed: `(left == right)`
  left: `"in \u{1b}[1;36m~\u{1b}[0m "`,
 right: `""`', tests/testsuite/directory.rs:19:5


failures:
    directory::directory_in_root
    directory::home_directory
```
Oh wait, my `home_directory` failure isn't even the same as yours. Hopefully the same root cause though.
@oblitum My original intention was to set up `starship`, `starship-git`, and `starship-bin`, but I haven't had time to get to all of them yet.

Gotta be honest, I'm a little stumped here. I can't reproduce this on my Arch machine (either in a clean chroot or in my actual environment) or on my MacBook (Catalina Beta).

@oblitum @lilyball Can you post screenshots for the output of `RUST_LOG=trace <path-to-failing-starship-binary> module directory --path=~`?

Here's what I see when I try that on the v0.11.0 source code from GitHub:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4605384/63294956-68b7f700-c280-11e9-8436-a2c0be1d57bc.png)

@chipbuster 
![JiXHzoW](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1269815/63303960-c4ea3d80-c2b7-11e9-959b-f12e9cba90fc.png)

I don't know about AUR, but in my case, the issue is the fact that `HOME` is set to a path that doesn't exist (`/homeless-shelter`, since I'm building in Nix), and this produces a panic with `--path=~`:

```
$ HOME=/homeless-shelter target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/starship module directory --path=~
thread 'main' panicked at 'Unable to read current directory: /homeless-shelter/', src/context.rs:61:17
note: Run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.
```

This doesn't explain my failure with `directory_in_root` though, unless there's some other env var that would affect that.

Actually maybe it does; in Nix I'm building in a sandboxed environment, and providing an invalid path to the `--path` parameter produces a similar exception. I bet the sandbox is preventing access to `/etc`:

```
$ RUST_LOG=trace HOME=/homeless-shelter target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/starship module directory --path=/etdf
 DEBUG starship::config > STARSHIP_CONFIG is not set
 DEBUG starship::config > Using default config path: /homeless-shelter/.config/starship.toml
 DEBUG starship::config > Unable to read config file content: 
No such file or directory (os error 2)
thread 'main' panicked at 'Unable to read current directory: /etdf', src/context.rs:61:17
note: Run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.
```

@lilyball We seem to have built a lot of tests based around the assumption that the filesystem would look similar to the Unix FHS. Between the Windows and Nix failures, we might have to revisit that assumption.

@chipbuster In my case, I do have a Unix FHS, but a combination of sandboxing and an intentionally-garbage `HOME` folder just means that the paths you're trying to test don't exist/aren't reachable.

In any case, it seems like a legitimate bug that `starship module directory --path=/something-that-doesn't-exist` will panic regardless of what the filesystem looks like.
@chipbuster the test failed in the same way with the patch applied.
@lilyball Yeah, that seems wrong. I'll open an issue against it.

@chipbuster these two lines were added to the end of the previous output, after the patch:

```
 DEBUG starship::modules::directory > Found repository root at "/home/francisco/"
 DEBUG starship::modules::directory > Repo folder name is "francisco"
```

@oblitum Perfect, that's what I was hoping for! 

The functionality of the directory module is fine (or at least, this test doesn't prove that it's conclusively broken), but `directory::home_directory()` expects the wrong output if your home directory is a git repository.

> if your home directory is a git repository

yep, it's indeed.

Sounds like the `starship` command might need a way for command-line arguments to override config, such that you can then disable things like `truncate_in_repo` for this.

Or it could use an arg / env var to override the config file location, and then you could write out a temporary config file and point it at that.

Huh, could have sworn I responded to this earlier...guess I imagined it.

@lilyball We do have such a construct in starship, but it's only usable in the testing interface (which is good enough for what we need it for).

@oblitum A binary release package is now available on AUR under `starship-bin`. I'll let it soak for a few days before I put it up on the ~wiki~ README (also need to figure out if I need to include the ISC license or not)
@chipbuster cool :)
